# mdbook-llms

---

# Getting started

Source: /mdbook-llms/getting-started.md

mdbook-llms is an [mdBook](https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/) 0.5 renderer that follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) convention. Alongside your HTML site it writes:

- [`llms.txt`](llms.txt): an index of every chapter, grouped by SUMMARY.md parts
- [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt): every chapter in reading order, in one file
- `<chapter>.md`: each chapter's Markdown at the path its HTML would use

## How it fits into mdBook

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SUMMARY.md + chapters] --> B["links preprocessor<br/>expands includes"]
    B --> C["strip-frontmatter + mermaid<br/>(HTML only)"]
    C --> D[html renderer] --> E[book/html/*.html]
    B --> F[mdbook-llms renderer]
    F --> G["llms.txt<br/>llms-full.txt<br/>chapter .md"]
    G -. written next to .-> E
```

The llms renderer reads the book before the HTML-only preprocessors run, so it sees chapter frontmatter and keeps Mermaid blocks as plain fenced code.

## Quick start

Install the binaries:

```sh
cargo install --locked mdbook-llms
```

Add the renderer and the frontmatter preprocessor to your `book.toml`:

```toml
[preprocessor.strip-frontmatter]

[output.html]

[output.llms]
```

Run `mdbook build`. The llms files appear in `book/html/`, next to the site.

This book is built the same way. See [Usage](/mdbook-llms/usage.md) for every option and [Contributing](/mdbook-llms/contributing.md) to work on the crate.

---

# Usage

Source: /mdbook-llms/usage.md

## Install

```sh
cargo install --locked mdbook-llms
```

From a local checkout, use `cargo install --path .` instead.

This installs two binaries: the `mdbook-llms` renderer and the `mdbook-strip-frontmatter` preprocessor. Both must be on your `PATH` when you run `mdbook build`.

## Configure

To generate only the llms files, list only this output. mdBook then skips HTML, CSS and JS completely, and the files land directly in `book/`:

```toml
[output.llms]
site-url = "https://example.com/my-book"
```

To publish alongside the site, keep both. The files go into `book/html/`, next to the HTML:

```toml
[preprocessor.strip-frontmatter]

[output.html]
site-url = "/my-book/"

[output.llms]
```

To skip HTML for one build without touching `book.toml`:

```sh
MDBOOK_OUTPUT='{"llms":{}}' mdbook build
```

## Options

All go under `[output.llms]`.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `site-url` | `output.html.site-url` | Prefix for links. Without either, links are relative to the output root. |
| `index` | `true` | Write `llms.txt`. |
| `full` | `true` | Write `llms-full.txt`. |
| `pages` | `true` | Write per-chapter `.md` files. When `false`, links point at `.html`. |
| `merge-into-html` | `true` | When HTML also runs, write into its directory rather than `book/llms/`. |
| `discovery-links` | `true` | When merged into the HTML output, add `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` and `<link rel="describedby">` to each HTML page, as [llms.txt v2](https://llmstxt.org/) recommends. |

## Frontmatter

A `description` key in a chapter's YAML frontmatter adds text to that chapter's `llms.txt` entry. Other keys are allowed and removed from all output:

```markdown
---
description: How to install the CLI
---

# Install
```

Add `[preprocessor.strip-frontmatter]` whenever HTML is enabled, or the HTML pages will show the block.

---

# Contributing

Source: /mdbook-llms/contributing.md

## Prerequisites

- Rust (edition 2024)
- [just](https://github.com/casey/just)
- [mdBook](https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/) 0.5
- [mdbook-mermaid](https://github.com/badboy/mdbook-mermaid) 0.17
- [cargo-audit](https://github.com/rustsec/rustsec/tree/main/cargo-audit)

`just setup` installs mdBook and mdbook-mermaid at the versions the docs are tested with.

## Layout

- `src/lib.rs`: config, link rewriting, frontmatter parsing and output writing.
- `src/main.rs`: the `mdbook-llms` renderer binary.
- `src/bin/mdbook-strip-frontmatter.rs`: the frontmatter preprocessor binary.
- `docs/`: this book, built with the renderer from the working tree.

## Workflow

Run `just` to list recipes. Before opening a pull request, run:

```sh
just fmt
just check
```

`check` runs `fmt-check`, `clippy` (warnings are errors), `test` and `audit`.

## Releases

Releases are made by [release-plz](https://release-plz.dev/) from [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), so prefix commit messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:` and so on, and mark breaking changes with `!` (e.g. `feat!:`). On each push to `main`, release-plz opens or updates a release PR that bumps the version and updates `CHANGELOG.md`. Merging it publishes the new version to crates.io through [trusted publishing](https://crates.io/docs/trusted-publishing), tags `vX.Y.Z` and creates a GitHub Release.

## Building the docs

```sh
just book
```

This builds the crate, puts `target/debug` first on `PATH` so mdBook uses the local binaries, and writes the site and llms files to `docs/book/`. Use `just serve` to preview the HTML.

`docs/snapshots/` holds the expected llms output for this book: `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and every per-chapter `.md` file. `just snapshot` builds into `target/book-snapshot/` and fails if any of them differ. After an intended change to the renderer or the docs, run `just snapshot-update` and review the diff.

---

# Example section

Source: /mdbook-llms/example/index.md

This section exists to show what mdbook-llms produces. Each chapter exercises one feature, and this page shows the resulting `llms.txt` for the whole book.

## What it shows

- **Parts**: `# Guide` and `# Example` in `SUMMARY.md` become `##` headings in `llms.txt`.
- **Section pages**: this file is `example/README.md`, so it is published as `example/index.md`.
- **Descriptions**: each chapter's frontmatter `description` follows its link.
- **Drafts**: `Draft chapter` has no file, so it is left out and [Included files](/mdbook-llms/example/included.md) moves up a level.

## Generated llms.txt

This is a committed snapshot of `book/html/llms.txt`. `just snapshot` fails if it no longer matches the build.

```text
# mdbook-llms

## Guide

- [Getting started](/mdbook-llms/getting-started.md): What mdbook-llms does and how to try it in a minute
- [Usage](/mdbook-llms/usage.md): Install, configure and the full list of `[output.llms]` options
- [Contributing](/mdbook-llms/contributing.md): Prerequisites, project layout and the just-based dev workflow

## Example

- [Example section](/mdbook-llms/example/index.md): A worked example showing each chapter's source next to the llms.txt it produces
  - [Frontmatter](/mdbook-llms/example/frontmatter.md): Frontmatter keys, and which ones reach the output
  - [Links](/mdbook-llms/example/links.md): How links between chapters are rewritten for each output
  - [Included files](/mdbook-llms/example/included.md): An {{#include}}-built chapter, listed one level up because its parent is a draft
```

---

# Frontmatter

Source: /mdbook-llms/example/frontmatter.md

This chapter's source opens with:

```yaml
---
description: Frontmatter keys, and which ones reach the output
tags:
  - example
  - frontmatter
---
```

- `description` is added to this chapter's line in `llms.txt`.
- `tags` is allowed and removed. It appears nowhere in the HTML or llms output.
- The block itself is removed from the HTML page by `strip-frontmatter` and from the Markdown output by `mdbook-llms`.

---

# Links

Source: /mdbook-llms/example/links.md

The source of this chapter links to other chapters by their `.md` paths:

- [Usage](/mdbook-llms/usage.md)
- [Usage options](/mdbook-llms/usage.md#options)
- [Frontmatter](/mdbook-llms/example/frontmatter.md)

In the output:

- **HTML** links point at `.html` pages, as usual for mdBook.
- **Per-chapter `.md` files** keep relative `.md` links. A link to a `README.md` chapter is changed to `index.md`, its published path.
- **`llms-full.txt`** has every chapter in one file, so the links are rewritten to work from there.

## Limitation: links to README.md

mdBook publishes a `README.md` chapter as `index.html`, but its HTML renderer does not rewrite links to it. A link like `[Overview](README.md)` becomes `README.html`, which does not exist, so it is broken in the HTML site.

mdbook-llms changes these links to `index.md` in its own output, but cannot fix the HTML. This book avoids linking to `README.md` chapters for that reason.

---

# Included files

Source: /mdbook-llms/example/included.md

mdbook-llms reads the book after mdBook's links preprocessor has run, so `{{#include}}` is already expanded in every output. This is this book's own `book.toml`, included from outside `src/`:

```toml
[book]
title = "mdbook-llms"
src = "src"

[preprocessor.strip-frontmatter]

[preprocessor.mermaid]
command = "mdbook-mermaid"

[output.html]
site-url = "/mdbook-llms/"
additional-js = ["mermaid.min.js", "mermaid-init.js"]

[output.llms]
```

## Including Rust source with anchors

An include can pull a named region out of a source file. `src/lib.rs` marks the renderer's config with `// ANCHOR: config` and `// ANCHOR_END: config`, and this page includes it with:

```text
{{#include ../../../src/lib.rs:config}}
```

mdBook drops the anchor lines, so the result is the real definition of every `[output.llms]` option and its default:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub struct Config {
    /// Write `llms.txt`.
    pub index: bool,
    /// Write `llms-full.txt`.
    pub full: bool,
    /// Write one `.md` file per chapter. When off, `llms.txt` links to `.html`.
    pub pages: bool,
    /// Prefix for links. Falls back to `output.html.site-url`.
    pub site_url: Option<String>,
    /// When the HTML renderer also runs, publish into its directory.
    pub merge_into_html: bool,
    /// When merged, add llms.txt v2 `alternate` and `describedby` links to HTML pages.
    pub discovery_links: bool,
}

impl Default for Config {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            index: true,
            full: true,
            pages: true,
            site_url: None,
            merge_into_html: true,
            discovery_links: true,
        }
    }
}
```

Anchors move with the code, unlike line ranges such as `lib.rs:15:40`. Because the snapshot test covers this page, a change to `Config` also shows up as a docs change.

## Drafts

In `SUMMARY.md` this chapter sits under `Draft chapter`, which has no file. Drafts get no page, so in `llms.txt` this chapter is listed one level up instead of disappearing.
